subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw add latency-aware Slack HTTP Request URL guidance or setup steering for hosted public-ingress deployments, or is the current deployment-shape transport guidance sufficient?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and Slack recommends HTTP for deployed production apps, but stronger setup guidance or default changes affect operator expectations and public-ingress requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and add latency-aware Slack docs/setup guidance recommending HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments.

options.title: Change setup steering
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode with operator and upgrade guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the existing transport table is sufficient and close this only after maintainers decide no latency-specific guidance is needed.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and add latency-aware Slack docs/setup guidance recommending HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the measurements, authored the partial Slack latency fixes, and scoped the remaining HTTP-guidance decision.
